answer: We model Sybil entry as a costly deviation from a strict Nash equilibrium, where each identity must post a dynamic opportunity-cost bond scaling with its marginal reward. The subgame-perfect slashing matrix imposes penalties that mirror deviation, ensuring a ripple of correlated losses across every duplicated node. Because aggregate bond losses exceed any spliced gain, identity multiplication yields negative expected payoff, making honest participation the unique equilibrium in the adversarial ocean.
